first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A planning service called Wedded Concierge that will organise a wedding in Portugal for Australian, US and UK couples, with one advisor. The top tells me the legal minimum is a month and that plenty of people just do a symbolic ceremony. It does not tell me what they charge or why I would use them instead of emailing a quinta myself.

attention_map.quote: a legal wedding in Portugal for foreign couples starts at least one month ahead
attention_map.why: A concrete, checkable fact up top instead of 'Europe's most romantic destination'. No superlatives, no countdown. That earns a scroll.

attention_map.quote: Planned by Wedded Concierge, with one Wedded Advisor from enquiry to the wedding weekend.
attention_map.why: This is where I expect numbers: how many Portugal weddings, how many years. It just repeats the hero sentence. A strip that looks like proof but says nothing makes me more suspicious, not less.

attention_map.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms dates and venues with you.
attention_map.why: 'Check your date' sounds like an availability check, but the small print admits it is just the enquiry form. At least they admit it.

attention_map.section: Fall for Portugal / Booking a Sintra Palace
attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra. Nothing may be fixed to the heritage. Monserrate's roof works run to early 2027.
attention_map.why: Telling me the catch on the palaces before I ask is the most trustworthy thing on the page. 'Early 2027' here and 'first quarter of 2027' elsewhere match.

Five cards, five times the same non-answer. Capacity is the first thing I compare across tabs. Also 'five regions, each with its own setting and airport', but Lisbon (LIS) is listed for both Lisbon/Sintra and Comporta, so it is four airports. Small, but it is exactly the kind of thing I check.

attention_map.section: What Your Wedded Advisor Checks in Every Venue Contract
attention_map.quote: exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill ... a buy-out is often charged separately from the venue fee ... whether each quote includes VAT, so totals compare like for like
attention_map.why: This is the hidden-cost list I came for, for venues at least. It is also the first real reason to use them. But it is all 'can', 'often', 'may', with no figures.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding: Marrying legally and Entry rules tabs
attention_map.quote: Legal and cost details checked October 2026, with sources named in each tab.
attention_map.why: Linked government sources per passport, the six-month window, the 18+ rule. Specific and checkable. Though 'The civil registry charges a fee for the ceremony' and 'a consular notarial fee applies' without amounts reads as if they did not bother looking it up.

attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things: your guest count, the region, the season, how many nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use.
attention_map.why: A heading that promises costs and a body with zero numbers. 'Legal and cost details checked October 2026' at the top of the tabs, then no cost details. That is the catch.

attention_map.section: See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes
attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package. Instead, your Wedded Advisor helps you plan a weekend around your guests, and it can include:
attention_map.why: Honest that there is no package, but 'can include' is not an inclusions list. Is the on-the-day coordinator yours, included, or an extra? Nothing says.
Free guest website. Free usually means the upsell comes later. Mild eye-roll.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding with One Wedded Advisor
attention_map.quote: Portugal properties are still being confirmed, so your Wedded Advisor tells you what applies to your dates.
attention_map.why: Why mention a perks programme that has nothing confirmed for Portugal? And still not a word on what this advisor costs me. The 'one contact instead of one conversation per venue' line is the only stated reason to book through them.

attention_map.quote: There is no single average: the cost depends on your guest count, the region, the season, the nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use.
attention_map.why: Legal and palace answers match the tabs word for word, which I check and appreciate. The cost answer dodges the question it repeats in its own heading.

attention_map.section: Read More About Weddings in Portugal
attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links where I wanted real weddings this team planned. Feels like a magazine, not a planner, and there is no real-weddings section at all.

questions_answered.question: What is NOT included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: There is no from price, no planner fee, no inclusions or exclusions list. The Costs tab and FAQ 4 give cost drivers with no figures. 'it can include' in the weekend list is not an inclusions list.

questions_answered.question: Are these facts consistent across the page?
questions_answered.evidence: Legal minimum (one month), six-month window, beach permit rule, five Parques de Sintra venues, Monserrate works and season advice all match across hero, tabs and FAQ. One slip: 'five regions, each with its own setting and airport' (s2 intro and FAQ 6) but only four airports, with Lisbon (LIS) serving two regions.

questions_answered.question: What proof is there that this team has done this venue before?
questions_answered.evidence: Proof strip has no numbers, no real weddings shown, no named advisor, no testimonial. 'Of all the Europe wedding destinations we plan' is a claim with nothing behind it. The only weddings linked are celebrity ones.

questions_answered.question: Why book through you and not the venue directly?
questions_answered.evidence: 'Your one contact at Wedded Concierge, instead of one conversation per venue' and the contract check for 'rooms, buy-outs, minimums and VAT'. A reason, but without knowing what it costs I cannot weigh it against going direct.

questions_answered.question: What happens if something goes wrong on the day?
questions_answered.evidence: Only 'An on-the-day coordinator' in a list of things a weekend 'can include'. Nothing about who is on site, backup plans, or responsibility. Wet-weather mentions ('plan a covered option', 'a plan for rain') are advice to me, not a promise from them.

objections_triggered.objection: From price with no inclusions list means hidden costs
objections_triggered.triggered_by: No price or fee anywhere; Costs tab fallback with no numbers; 'There is no single average'; 'The civil registry charges a fee for the ceremony'; 'a consular notarial fee applies'
'Planned by Wedded Concierge, with one Wedded Advisor...' in the proof slot; 'Of all the Europe wedding destinations we plan'; no real weddings; celebrity article row
'five regions, each with its own setting and airport' versus four airports listed, with LIS shared by two regions

objections_triggered.objection: Vague answers on things I compare (capacity, perks, service)
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'Guests: Ask your Wedded Advisor' on all five region cards; 'Portugal properties are still being confirmed'
'An on-the-day coordinator' listed only under 'it can include'

trust_signals_noticed: Palace booking conditions disclosed up front, including state-event cancellations and Monserrate scaffolding
Venue contract checklist: exclusive-use rooms, buy-outs, per-guest minimums, VAT
Linked official sources per passport and 'checked October 2026'
Legal facts consistent between tabs and FAQ
'There is no set Portugal package' instead of a fake package
Clear statement that every enquiry goes to Wedded Concierge
turn_offs_noticed: A proof strip with no proof
A Costs heading with no costs
'Ask your Wedded Advisor' used as the answer to capacity five times
Celebrity wedding links in place of real weddings
'Start for free' hinting at a later upsell
A perks programme mentioned with nothing confirmed

emotional_response.overall: Grudging respect for the homework, then irritation. It is the most honest page of my four tabs on the legal side, and the least forthcoming on money.
emotional_response.strongest_positive: The palace conditions and the venue contract checklist
emotional_response.strongest_negative: No fee, no figures, no proof, so the enquiry form is where the real price conversation starts, which is exactly what I do not want

payload.decision_reason: I will only enquire when no cost question is left open, and here every cost question is open: no planner fee, no inclusions, no ranges, not even the registry fee. Add zero proof that they have planned a Portugal wedding, and I cannot compare this like for like with the other tabs that at least show a starting price. The good legal content is on the government sites they link, so I do not need to come back here for it.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Okay, this is properly researched, I'll give them that. They even tell me the palace can be cancelled for a state event. But what's the catch? I've read the whole thing and I still don't know what these people charge, what's included, or whether they've ever actually done a wedding in Portugal. The 'proof' bar is just the slogan again, the costs tab has no costs, and every guest question is 'ask your advisor'. That's how you end up on a sales call. Other tabs have a number. Closing this one.
